The derivation begins with defining the Q-factor n as the ratio of co-fraternity variance to population variance. From the excerpt, n is constrained to be ≤ 1, implying that co-fraternity variance cannot exceed population variance. For stature, the ratio is empirically determined as 15:17, yielding n ≈ 0.882. This value is compared against a hypothetical 0.9 estimate, which is rejected due to environmental influences. The variability is decomposed into fraternal (shared ancestry/nurture) and inter-fraternity (diverse ancestry/nurture) components. The former affects all co-fraternities similarly, while the latter introduces heterogeneity across groups. Environmental factors—such as parental vigor and family traditions—modulate these effects, leading to higher variability in non-vigorous lineages. These considerations inform the breakdown regime where n > 1 or inconsistent variance ratios signal model misalignment.
